They might give us a star.
Viktor Petrovich, good evening.
We want to thank you for last night's dinner.
Do not mention it, it is my job.
By the way, regarding work.
I want to offer you to become my personal chef.
I understand you are used to other scales.
You will have a worthy salary, equipment, and staff.
And you will have only two regular guests.
Me and my wife.
Alright, I will think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'my', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Боже мой, спасибо вам огромное!

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.
